answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a bond in a scarce token, then slash that bond when the identity is caught duplicating claims or coordinating votes with linked accounts. A bridge contract can hold the bond and release it only after a long, public participation period, so creating a swarm ties up capital and exposes it to evidence-based challenges. The attacker pays opportunity cost on every account, while a pearl of reputation earned over time cannot be copied across identities on a dune of cheap accounts.
